display.purpose: The prep surface's single large editable mood-name heading (34px/30px compact). The live view uses Oswald more broadly for its own display titles (.mood h2, #standby h2) at different, surface-specific sizes -- see DESIGN.md Typography.

brand.purpose: The "SOUNDSCAPE" app-bar wordmark. Editor renders it 16px/0.18em; live-view renders the same wordmark 13px/0.28em — a known inconsistency, not two intentional variants.

title.purpose: Section and panel headings (grid heading, properties inspector, drawer heading). No explicit line-height is set in source; frontmatter records 'normal'.

body.purpose: Default UI text: inputs, buttons, running copy. No explicit line-height is set at this level in source (frontmatter 'normal'); .sound-meta specifically sets 1.5.

label.purpose: Metadata, field labels, library captions -- weight 400, line-height 1.5 where set (.sound-meta). kbd is the one label-sized element using weight 500 instead.

shadows.name: drawer-rise
shadows.purpose: Cast upward from the library drawer as it slides up over the editor; the only shadow on a surface that detaches from normal layout flow.

shadows.name: toast-float
shadows.purpose: Cast downward from the toast as it floats above the transport bar.

shadows.name: active-mood-lift
shadows.purpose: live-view.html only: cast under .mood.big .frame, the sounding/hovered mood, to lift it off the feed. Not part of the prep surface's flat-until-detached pattern.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Shared easing (--ease in the editor, --ease-out in live-view) for hover, selection, disclosure, and drawer-reveal transitions.

motion.name: duration-hover
motion.purpose: Card border-color/background hover and artwork brightness/filter transitions.

motion.name: duration-reveal
motion.purpose: Library drawer height/transform/opacity reveal. Opening: visibility becomes visible immediately (0s delay). Closing: visibility switches to hidden only after the 230ms slide-out completes (transition-delay 230ms on visibility), so the drawer stays painted through its closing animation; the controller disables interaction immediately via inert.

motion.name: context-change
motion.purpose: Keyframe fade applied to the sound grid when switching mood/scene context, to avoid a hard content pop.

motion.name: reduced-motion-override
motion.value: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce collapses all animation/transition durations to 1ms and forces scroll-behavior: auto
motion.purpose: Accessibility floor; applies globally, no exceptions.

breakpoints.name: compact-height
breakpoints.purpose: Vertical-space accommodation for short desktop windows: smaller art, tighter padding, shorter card minimums. Not a mobile breakpoint.

breakpoints.name: inspector-narrow
breakpoints.purpose: Narrows the properties inspector (288px to 264px) and collapses the library results grid to 1 column.

breakpoints.name: grid-two-col
breakpoints.purpose: Drops the sound grid from 3 to 2 columns on narrower desktop windows; hides the grid-heading hint and preview-volume readout.

breakpoints.name: library-wide
breakpoints.purpose: Expands the library drawer's results grid to 3 columns (2 when the import panel is open).

narrative.overview:
The system is named after its own two load-bearing tokens: --void (#0a0a0c), the near-black ground everything sits on, and --ink (#f5f4f0), the single off-white that carries text, icons, borders-at-rest, and every active/selected state. The palette is a shared near-monochrome void/ink core: a few nearby neutral panels (--panel) plus ink-alpha layers (--surface, --surface-raised, the --line family) sit close to, but are not strict alpha derivations of, void/ink -- there is no chromatic accent anywhere in the system. The one deliberate exception is a muted coral (--error) reserved exclusively for invalid input; it is a feedback signal, not an accent.

This is a control surface for a tool that must recede: the GM glances at it between seconds of narration, and the artwork on each mood/sound tile is what actually carries scene color and emotional read. The chrome's job is to stay legible and quiet underneath that imagery -- restrained hairline borders, a condensed display face for mood/context titles, and one compact UI face for controls and metadata. These are clickable browser prototypes (prototype/mood-editor.html, prototype/live-view.html) built to preview a native macOS gpui application; the browser is a preview medium only, and the owner implements the real UI in Rust. Interactive states (selection, hover, drag, search, import forms) work in-prototype, but playback and media imports are explicitly simulated -- no audio plays and no files are downloaded.
keyCharacteristics: Two-color core (void + ink); nearby neutral panels and ink-alpha layers build the rest, with no chromatic accent.
Artwork supplies scene color; UI chrome never competes with it.
Oswald carries the wordmark and mood/context display titles (prep's one editable heading, live view's mood titles and standby heading); everything else is Space Grotesk.
Mostly flat, tonal depth in prep (hairline borders, alpha layering); the live view's active mood frame and two detached prep overlays (drawer, toast) are the system's only shadows.
Muted coral exists for exactly one job: invalid input feedback.

rules.name: The Two-Color Rule
rules.body: --void and --ink form the shared near-monochrome core; nearby neutral panels and ink-alpha layers provide depth. Do not introduce a separate editor accent: use contrast, inversion, or artwork instead of new chrome hues.

rules.name: The Coral Exception Rule
rules.body: --error (#efab99, a muted coral) marks invalid input (aria-invalid="true" borders, .field-feedback text) and nothing else. It is not a brand color, not a success/status color, and must never be reused for emphasis or decoration.

rules.name: The Display-Titles Rule
rules.body: Oswald is reserved for the wordmark and for mood/context display titles -- the editor's one editable mood-name heading at prep time, and the live view's mood and standby titles during play. Controls, metadata, and body copy are Space Grotesk everywhere.

rules.name: The Flat-Until-Detached Rule
rules.body: In the prep surface, everything that lives in the normal layout -- cards, tabs, bars, the inspector -- stays flat; shadow is reserved for the two surfaces that physically leave the flow (drawer, toast). The live view's active-mood lift is a separate, surface-specific exception for its one emphasized state, not a contradiction of prep's flatness.

dos: Do keep --void (#0a0a0c) and --ink (#f5f4f0) as the shared near-monochrome core; build the rest from nearby neutral panels and ink-alpha layers, with no chromatic accent (The Two-Color Rule).
Do let artwork supply all scene color; UI chrome stays void/ink regardless of mood or scene.

Do reserve Oswald for the wordmark and mood/context display titles -- the editor's one editable heading, the live view's mood and standby titles -- and keep everything else in Space Grotesk (The Display-Titles Rule).

Do keep motion surface-specific: prep uses 140-230ms control/reveal transitions on cubic-bezier(.22, 1, .36, 1) and ~1ms under prefers-reduced-motion; the live feed has its own longer artwork/list transitions.
Do put a 2px solid ink :focus-visible outline (2-3px offset) on every interactive element; never rely on color change alone for focus.
donts: Don't introduce olive/green chrome or a separate "editor" accent palette -- the editor and live view share one near-black/white language.
Don't promote --error (#efab99, muted coral) beyond invalid-input feedback; it is not a status, success, or brand color (The Coral Exception Rule).
Don't treat this as a phone/mobile product. Design and verify desktop window resizing; 1024-2128px is the current checked range, not a declared native-window minimum.

Don't add drop shadows to prep's cards, tiles, or tabs at rest or on hover -- depth there comes from border/background steps, not elevation; this does not extend to the live view's active-mood lift shadow, which is its own surface's exception (The Flat-Until-Detached Rule).

Don't treat the mood-preparation surface's 3-/2-column grid or its bottom library+transport stack as a universal product layout requirement -- that composition belongs to its own surface brief, not this system-wide document.
